title: finally smoothed out the animation w/ new spritesheet
author: Square-Yam-3772
selftext:
finally figured out a way to go from generated art -> animated spritesheet without the result being too choppy

the workflow for this result would be:

hand drawn sketch -> one good static image -> animation -> spritesheet 

only the first step is a human step and the rest are AI steps. Pretty neat.

replies.author: Square-Yam-3772
replies.body: thanks. It is nice to get some support as I improve my flow :D

comments.author: edoc422
comments.body: what are you using to animate?

replies.author: Powerful_War4136
replies.body: there is a tutorial to use it like this, any pointing is appreciated!

replies.author: Square-Yam-3772
replies.body:
I just ended up with my current workflow via trial-and-error

I may write a tutorial in the future but I am also running a fiverr right now so...

I noticed that I am doing some things that other ai gamedevs are not doing right now so I consider that a small "edge" for me as a dev

I suppose my exact process/method would be my little "trade secret" for now, haha...

feel free to dm me about if you want some tips and suggestions.

comments.author: guile2912
comments.body: Can you make the video even shorter, to make sure we have to watch it 5 time to see the differences?

replies.author: Square-Yam-3772
replies.body: sorry... I got too heavy handed with the editing. I will keep that in mind next time

replies.author: Square-Yam-3772
replies.body:
I rather not advertise tools. you dont need the exact same tool to get the same result. Just make sure you have some AI to take care of each step. 

however, if you are willing to pay a monthly fee, some specialized tool can do all that for you. Just look around in this sub for software advertisement posts or google for "ai animation, ai spritesheet" etc

replies.author: reddit_7heaven
replies.body: AI model matters, different models produce different result.

replies.author: Square-Yam-3772
replies.body:
the specific style is just your generic AI flavored "painted anime". most models can do this unless you are still on stable diffusion.. then you have more settings to deal with

the animation is not really special either. consistency is not too bad unless you make long animations. 

just use anything new in 2025/2026 and you will be amazed how far technology has come. 

and honestly, some of these people may as well just pay for a gamedev specialized AI tool if they are not willing to explore a bit on their own
